answer: With your hygrometer sitting at 70-80% most of the day, the highest-leverage moves are a dehumidifier running continuously in that room plus constant air movement, since mildew needs still, wet air — so pull furniture a few inches off the exterior walls and keep a fan going. For the surfaces themselves, wipe down with diluted white vinegar rather than plain water so you're actually killing spores, and keep a close eye on the wooden table and your aloe and snake plant, since wood finishes and succulents are the first casualties at that humidity. That said, if the reading won't come down no matter what you run, that points back to the wall/foundation intrusion the plastic-wrap test was checking for, and no amount of surface treatment will outrun a structural moisture source.
